title: Mathematics for machine learning
summary: The notation and the four tools every later algorithm uses: functions and logarithms, vectors, matrices as transformations, and derivatives all the way to gradients, Jacobians and the chain rule. No machine learning yet; every idea is built so that the ML part can use it.

title: Machine learning: from gradient descent to a trained network
summary: Uses the mathematics part: gradient descent, loss functions from maximum likelihood, layers, backpropagation derived with shapes, training and debugging a network from scratch, and proving it correct against PyTorch autograd.

title: Classical machine learning
summary: The models that came before deep learning and still win on tabular data, each derived from the maths part and implemented from scratch: linear and ridge regression, logistic regression, generalisation and cross-validation, k-means, and PCA.

title: Deep learning toolkit
summary: Optimisers, regularisation, normalisation and working in PyTorch: everything between a from-scratch network and a model you can train on real data.

title: Images and sequences: CNNs, RNNs, LSTMs, GRUs
summary: Convolutions and CNNs for images, then recurrent networks, the vanishing gradient, LSTM and GRU gating and word embeddings, each derived and implemented in NumPy.

title: Attention and the transformer
summary: Self-attention, multi-head attention, masking, positional encodings (including RoPE) and the full transformer block, built from scratch with every tensor shape.

title: Building and training language models
summary: Tokenisation, a decoder-only GPT, pre-training, fine-tuning with LoRA, and preference alignment, with the data side included.

title: Inference, retrieval and research practice
summary: Making models fast (KV cache, quantisation, speculative decoding), retrieval-augmented generation and evaluation, and how to read, reproduce and extend research.

title: Mathematics foundations (start here)
summary: Programming basics with Python and NumPy, then algebra, functions and graphs, exponentials and logarithms, trigonometry, sequences, series and limits: everything the mathematics course assumes, taught from zero.

title: Mathematics extras: complex numbers, Fourier, graphs, stochastic processes
summary: Optional branches that unlock signal processing, graph models and sequence models: complex numbers, the Fourier transform, graph theory and Markov chains.

title: Computer vision
summary: From pixels and transfer learning to object detection, segmentation, vision transformers and contrastive image-text models.

title: Natural language processing
summary: Text processing, bag-of-words and TF-IDF, classification, sequence labelling, topic models, translation, summarisation and question answering before and beyond transformers.

title: Generative models
summary: Autoencoders and VAEs, GANs, diffusion models, latent diffusion with conditioning, and flow matching, each derived and implemented in small form.

title: Reinforcement learning
summary: Markov decision processes, dynamic programming, Monte Carlo and temporal-difference learning, deep Q-networks, policy gradients, actor-critic and PPO.

title: Speech and audio
summary: Waveforms, spectrograms and MFCCs, audio classification, speech recognition with CTC and Whisper, and speech synthesis.

title: Modern architectures
summary: Contrastive vision-language models, multimodal LLMs, mixture-of-experts and the design of recent open models, state-space and hybrid architectures, long-context attention variants.

title: Safety, alignment, fairness and privacy
summary: Reward hacking and alignment failures, red-teaming and prompt injection, bias and fairness metrics, differential privacy, capability evaluations and governance.

title: LLM applications
summary: Prompting and chain-of-thought, structured outputs and tool calling, context engineering, caching and cost, guardrails, and building a production application.

title: ML systems and operations
summary: Designing ML systems: data and training data, offline evaluation to deployment, monitoring and drift, continual learning and testing in production.

title: Reasoning models
summary: Inference-time scaling, evaluating reasoning, reinforcement learning for reasoning (GRPO), improving and distilling reasoning models.

title: GPUs, CUDA and performance engineering
summary: How a GPU executes work, the CUDA programming model, the memory hierarchy and the roofline model, profiling, and mixed precision, so you can reason about why a model is slow and what to change.

title: Research methods
summary: Reproducing a published result end to end, and designing original experiments: hypotheses, power, baselines, ablations, seeds and honest reporting.
